properties.electronic_state: singlet, formal Cr-Cr sextuple bond (sigma2 pi4 delta4); strongly multireference, 12 near-degenerate 3d-derived bonding electrons
properties.accessible_reason: No trustworthy potential energy curve / bond dissociation energy at the only allowed levels of theory (GFN2-xTB, PM7). Both are single-determinant semi-empirical methods with no static correlation and no explicit 3d-3d multiple bonding. GFN2-xTB gives r_e 2.1289 A and De 142.2 kcal/mol (experiment ~1.679 A, 33-35 kcal/mol), and is spin-restricted (xtb 6.5.0 prints no multiplicity, Nalpha-Nbeta or S**2). PM7's energy is not a single-valued function of r: at the fixed geometry r = 2.50 A the default RHF solution gives 0.802503 Eh while scf=qc gives 1.360301 Eh (350 kcal/mol apart), and the PM7 asymptotic limit is not size-consistent (septet dimer at 10 and 20 A = 0.468668 Eh sits 104 kcal/mol ABOVE 2 x E(Cr atom, 7S) = 0.302784 Eh; at 15 A it is 20 kcal/mol lower than at 10/20 A). PM7 also treats Cr as a 6-valence-electron ZDO centre, so a 3+3 (sextuple-bond) dissociation is not representable. The singlet is also the wrong state at PM7/UPM7, which puts the septet below the singlet everywhere (by 83-260 kcal/mol).
properties.bond_dissociation_energy_kcal_mol: not declared - not computable to trustworthy accuracy with the allowed methods (xTB/PM7). Exploratory only, all different: PM7 5.0 (6 A supermolecule) / 9.4 (15 A) / 29.7 (10-20 A) / 40.4 (Cr 7S + Cr 1S) / 74.4 (2 x Cr 7S); GFN2-xTB 142.2 (vs isolated Cr atom), D0 141.3. The 29.7 kcal/mol PM7 value's apparent agreement with experiment (33-35 kcal/mol = 1.45 eV) is coincidental and must not be used. See accessible=false.
properties.experimental_reference: r_e ~1.679 A, D_e ~1.45 eV = 33-35 kcal/mol (strongly multireference; used only as a sanity scale, not as evidence)

method_PM7_RPM7_multiplicity1.method: Gaussian 16, #p sp PM7 (RPM7), gas phase, charge 0, multiplicity 1, rigid Cr-Cr distances
method_PM7_RPM7_multiplicity1.caveat: Energies are NOT a single-valued function of r (multiple SCF solution families; the wiggles e.g. 2.90 -> 3.00 A (+95 kcal/mol) and 2.60 -> 2.65 -> 2.70 A are solution switches, not chemistry). The PM7 mult-1 'optimum' converged to r = 4.0133 A (NImag 0), which is two non-interacting singlet Cr atoms (2 x E(Cr, m1) = 0.668364 Eh), not a Cr-Cr bond.

method_PM7_UPM7_multiplicity7.method: Gaussian 16, #p PM7 (UPM7), gas phase, charge 0, multiplicity 7 (septet); scf=qc used where the default SCF diverged
method_PM7_UPM7_multiplicity7.caveat: Genuine septet minimum at r = 2.6553 A, E = 0.421269 Eh, 577.17 cm-1, 0 imaginary. <S**2> = 12.05 at the minimum but 13.24 at 6 A and 13.00 at 15 A (spin contamination). Asymptotic limit not size-consistent (see accessible_reason).

method_GFN2_xTB_restricted_multiplicity1.method: xtb 6.5.0, GFN2-xTB, charge 0, --uhf 0 (spin-restricted; no real open-shell/septet solution available)
method_GFN2_xTB_restricted_multiplicity1.caveat: Smooth but quantitatively wrong: r_e = 2.1289 A (opt, 581.50 cm-1, 0 imaginary, Wiberg BO 4.28), De = 142.2 kcal/mol (~4x experiment). Atom reference is a spin/orbital-averaged 4s2 3d4.8 ensemble, not 3d5 4s1 7S.

properties.evidence_log_note: Gaussian PM7 logs are the parseable evidence; the xtb GFN2 stdout and summary are supporting raw output (not in ORCA/Gaussian format).

properties.electronic_state: septet (six unpaired electrons, <S**2> = 12.05 at the minimum)
properties.accessible_reason: A genuine PM7 stationary point exists (r = 2.6553 A, 577.17 cm-1, 0 imaginary) but its dissociation energy is unquantifiable: the PM7 asymptotic limit is not size-consistent for Cr2 (10/20 A septet points sit 104 kcal/mol above 2 x E(Cr, 7S); a spin-accessible atomic sum is even below the computed dimer, which is variationally impossible). No GFN2 septet exists (xtb 6.5.0 GFN2 is spin-restricted; its --uhf 6 runs are occupation-constrained, not a septet).
properties.relative_energy_vs_singlet_pm7_kcal_mol: UPM7 places the septet below the singlet at every distance: -82.9 (1.80 A), -228.0 (2.50 A), -248.5 (2.60 A), -148.9 (3.00 A), -260.6 (6.00 A, qc); the requested singlet is not the PM7 ground state.
properties.bond_dissociation_energy_kcal_mol: not declared (accessible=false; PM7 not size-consistent for Cr2)
properties.role_note: Node role 'intermediate' is a schema convenience only: mechanistically this is a distinct electronic state reached by a spin change, not an intermediate on the singlet dissociation path (Supervisor review dec_79717799674e47e48ee86e5d8c0689cb).
properties.caveats: Shape and the 577.17 cm-1 mode are not trustworthy beyond sign/order of magnitude, because the Hamiltonian is not size-consistent for Cr2 (10/20 A septet 0.468668 Eh vs 2 x E(Cr,7S) = 0.302784 Eh).

properties.electronic_state: each Cr atom in its 3d5 4s1 7S3 ground state; the singlet Cr2 curve correlates with the S = 0 coupling of two 7S atoms, so a septet-coupled asymptote (as computed) is an upper-bound-style reference, not the state-matched one
properties.accessible_reason: The separated-atom limit itself is trivially computable and was computed (PM7 septet supermolecule at 20 A: E = 0.468668 Eh, 0.0000 cm-1, 0 imaginary; mult-1 counterpart at 6 A: E = 0.844462 Eh, 25.69 cm-1, 0 imaginary). What is inaccessible is the DEPTH of the well above it - see the Cr2 node.
properties.note: Asymptote mismatch between isolated-atom sums and large-r supermolecules is itself the size-consistency failure documented on the Cr2 node.
properties.size_consistency_note: The 20 A supermolecule (0.468668 Eh) does not reproduce 2 x E(Cr,7S) = 0.302784 Eh (104 kcal/mol), 10 and 20 A disagree with 15 A (0.436198 Eh, <S**2> 13.000 vs 12.244), and the singlet Cr2 curve correlates with the S=0 coupling of two 7S atoms while these asymptotes are septet-coupled: no BDE may be derived through this node.

edges.channel: homolytic Cr-Cr bond dissociation (singlet, formal sextuple bond)
edges.barrier_kcal_mol_note: barrierless - homolytic cleavage of a single diatomic bond has no first-order saddle; no barrier is declared and no TS exists
edges.accessible_reason: The step has no transition state (barrierless monotonic stretch), and the product-side energy scale is unusable at PM7/xTB, so no barrier or reaction energy can be declared for this edge. The bond_changes are unambiguous (the only Cr-Cr bond is fully cleaved).

edges.channel: homolytic Cr-Cr bond dissociation (high-spin septet channel)
edges.barrier_kcal_mol_note: barrierless; no TS located or expected
edges.accessible_reason: See Cr2_septet_state: PM7 is not size-consistent for Cr2, so no reaction energy is declared.
edges.favored_note: PM7/UPM7 places the septet below the singlet at every computed distance (by 83-260 kcal/mol), so at PM7 level the high-spin channel is the lower one; this is a statement about the method's preference, not a trustworthy reaction energy (see accessible_reason).
